pr.title: Use delayed bug for normalization errors in drop elaboration
pr.description:
Normalization can fail due to a lot of different earlier errors, so just use span_delayed_bug if normalization failed.

Closes #137287 
Closes #135668

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: use crate::elaborate_drop::{DropElaborator, DropFlagMode, DropStyle, Unwind, elaborate_drop};
The PR changes drop-elaboration normalization error handling and regression tests; ElaborateDrops is the concrete MIR pass implementing this path.

analysis.originalLogic: In `DropCtxt::elaborate_drop` within the `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass, after fixing the typing env to `PostAnalysis`, the pass normalizes each field type via `tcx.try_normalize_erasing_regions(self.elaborator.typing_env(), f.ty(tcx, args))`. On `Err(_)`, the original code built `Ty::new_error(self.tcx(), self.elaborator.body().tainted_by_errors.expect("Error in drop elaboration not found by dropck."))`, i.e. it assumed that any normalization failure here must have been already recorded as a body taint by dropck and panicked otherwise.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: When `try_normalize_erasing_regions` returned `Err(_)`, the historical code did NOT recover; it invoked `.tainted_by_errors.expect("Error in drop elaboration not found by dropck.")` on the elaborated body. For inputs where normalization fails because of earlier unrelated errors that dropck did not record as body taint (e.g. type-alias-impl-trait / unconstrained opaque type, conflicting trait impls, `compile_error!` in async code), `tainted_by_errors` is `None`, so the `expect` panics and produces an ICE ("Failed to normalize ...", "Error in drop elaboration not found by dropck."). The corrected transformation instead constructs an error type using `self.tcx().dcx().span_delayed_bug(self.elaborator.body().span, "Error normalizing in drop elaboration.")` rather than asserting a tainted body.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source that reaches MIR drop elaboration after analysis (TypingMode::PostAnalysis) and whose field types contain aliases/projections/opaque types that fail to normalize, while the compilation has already emitted errors that are not necessarily recorded in `body.tainted_by_errors` by dropck. Concrete regression inputs: (1) `type Alias<T> = impl Sized;` (unconstrained opaque type / `impl Trait` in type aliases) combined with a blanket `impl<T> Trait<T> for T` and a conflicting `impl<T> Trait<T> for defining_scope::Alias<T>`, plus a `cast` function returning `Container<T,T>` from `Container<Alias<T>,T>`; (2) async code with `compile_error!("bonjour")` and generic `impl Sized` return/associated types. Normal compilations without prior errors and types that normalize are outside the failing trigger.
analysis.summary: Bug fix (ICE, not an optimization): `ElaborateDrops` must not assume a failed field-type normalization implies `body.tainted_by_errors` is set. Normalization can fail due to many earlier errors that dropck did not taint, so the pass should recover with an error type and `span_delayed_bug` instead of panicking via `expect`. Regression tests promote two `tests/crashes/*` cases to `tests/ui/drop/drop_elaboration_with_errors{2,3}.rs` with explicit expected diagnostics.
analysis.trigger: `try_normalize_erasing_regions` returns `Err(_)` inside `ElaborateDrops` while `body.tainted_by_errors` is `None` because the normalization failure stems from earlier errors not registered by dropck.
preconditions: MIR drop elaboration runs under TypingMode::PostAnalysis, so `assert_eq!(self.elaborator.typing_env().typing_mode, ty::TypingMode::PostAnalysis)` holds.
The crate already has errors (e.g. unconstrained opaque type, type-alias-impl-trait instability, conflicting implementations, compile_error!) that allow analysis to continue.
Dropck did not delete the MIR body / did not set `body.tainted_by_errors`, so it remains `None`.
At least one elaborated field type fails `try_normalize_erasing_regions`.
pitfalls: Assuming every normalization failure in drop elaboration was already caught and recorded by `compute_drop_data`/dropck; the old comment explicitly documented this assumption and it is false.
Using `expect`/panic-based assertions for error-recovery paths: normalization failure is not itself a compiler bug and should not ICE.
Treating this as an optimization PR; it is a confirmed ICE bug fix with no optimization correctness change.
Assuming `body.tainted_by_errors` is the authoritative signal for normalization failures; it can be `None` even with prior errors.
Only testing with a single error kind; failures arise from multiple unrelated earlier error classes (TAIT, conflicting impls, compile_error!).
analysis.testStrategy: UI regression tests: promote crash repros into `tests/ui/drop/drop_elaboration_with_errors2.rs` (replace `//@ known-bug: #137287` with `// Regression test for #137287`, keep the `impl Sized` type alias, conflicting blanket/opaque impls, and `cast` return-type mismatch) and `drop_elaboration_with_errors3.rs` (edition 2021, async fns, `compile_error!("bonjour")`, add `fn main() {}`). Add `.stderr` files with `//~^`/`//~|` annotations asserting exact errors: E0658 `impl Trait` in type aliases is unstable, E0119 conflicting implementations, "unconstrained opaque type", E0308 mismatched types; and `error: bonjour` for the second. Success criterion is a clean diagnostic report with no panic/ICE from drop elaboration. Do not claim these were executed here; no compiler was built.
